thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: 3x increase in /v1/generate 5xx errors from inference-runtime in prod (us-west). Error rate >20% for the last 2m. Paging on-call.

oncall-bot: @channel incident declared: inference-runtime elevated 5xx. Severity: P1. Runbook: inference-runtime -> triage -> mitigation.

alex_m: I'm seeing spike on gateway 502/504 and model-runner 5xx. Started ~10:02 UTC. Routing shows multiple pods in runner pool returning 500.

maria_r: linked traces: https://trace.redwood/infer/trace/0xabc123 — majority of failures are kernel OOMs inside the runner container, followed by segfaults.

jamie_t: Confirmed. Logs from one affected pod: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:03:12Z] runtime: panic: segfault at 0x0
[2026-03-15T10:03:12Z] goroutine 42 [running]:
#0 0x7f6a1b2c in attention_kernel()
#1 0x7f6a3c4f in execute_forward()
```
Container restarted by kubelet, then started serving but hit OOM within 30s.

siva: @maria_r can you paste the dmesg / kernel OOM lines from node? Need to know if it's host OOM or container cgroup.

maria_r: dmesg snippet: "[   12.345678] Kernel panic - not syncing: Out of memory: Killed process 2345 (model_runner) total-vm:5120000kB..." Looks like host OOM on a few nodes, not just container kill.

lisa_k: Customer traffic: top-10 tenants saw increased 502/503s; top affected tenant is acme-inc with ~1.2k requests/min. CS is already pinged.

alex_m: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) put affected pool into maintenance (drain) 2) route traffic to warm fallback pool with smaller model (compat variant) 3) throttle burst traffic via gateway rate limit 4) scale up node pool if capacity available.

jamie_t: I'm going to pause new assignments to this runner pool and flip routing to fallback model variant. Will update in 30s.

oncall-bot: Action: set runner-pool-usw to cordon/drain.

jamie_t: Done — started drain, new requests routed to fallback variant redwood/gpt-small-compat. Gateway rule applied: 30s rolling shift.

maria_r: After routing change, 5xx rate dropped to 3% over 2m. Latency slightly higher for those customers (~+120ms).

alex_m: Next: collect core dumps from crashed pods for postmortem. Enable core collector on affected nodes, set sysctl kernel.core_pattern to capture. Also capture full `free -h` and `nvidia-smi` snapshots.

jamie_t: I'm seeing one node with persistent memory pressure: /dev/shm usage at 100% and kernel OOMs. Node ID: ip-10-0-45-12. Quiescing jobs there.

siva: I'll run a live check to see if the host has runaway pinned GPU memory or a leaking process.

siva: Findings: stale processes from previous jobs held GPU memory (pid 9987). Killed them, freed ~28GB GPU mem. Restarted model runner on that node in isolation.

lisa_k: Customer impact update: Acme reported 14% error rate peak, now down to 2%. CS notified customers on affected tenants; ops note shared.

alex_m: Root cause hypothesis (working): regression in a recent attention optimization kernel in v2.3.1 that can allocate unbounded pinned memory under specific sequence-length patterns, leading to host OOM and segfaults. The rollout started ~02:00 UTC in canary but hit prod yesterday 09:58 UTC.

maria_r: Reproducer: sequence_len ~8192 + certain prompt patterns — alloc path uses huge pages fallback then into pinned allocator. Running a reproducer job now.

jamie_t: Mitigation plan: 1) rollback runner image to v2.3.0 for affected pool (done) 2) keep fallback routing for 10m post-rollback 3) patch in v2.3.2 to fix allocator checks before wide rollout.

oncall-bot: Action: rollback image on runner-pool-usw to v2.3.0 initiated by jamie_t.

jamie_t: Rollback completed across drained pool and we marked nodes for reprovision after full cleanup. 5xx rate back to baseline ~0.5%.

alex_m: Post-rollback: scheduling a controlled rollout of v2.3.2 to canary only after patch and additional e2e reproducer tests.

siva: Collected artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/4920012345/artifacts/ (core dumps, dmesg, nvidia-smi, runner logs). Saved checksums.

lisa_k: CS note: drafted message to affected customers explaining mitigation and ETA for root cause fix.

maria_r: Next steps for on-call: run full nightly mem-leak scans in canary, expand alerting to detect host swap pressure and /dev/shm saturation. Add soft limit on sequence length via gateway config to prevent immediate recurrence.

alex_m: Thanks all. I'll file a postmortem ticket and assign action items (kernel allocator guard, reproduce test, alert tuning, customer follow-up).

oncall-bot: Incident closed to P2 at 10:41 UTC. Please add any follow-ups to the incident board. :white_check_mark:

lisa_k: Adding final note: total customer-facing window ~38m, peak error 20% for top tenants; mitigated by routing/fallback + rollback.

jamie_t: Leaving handoff for next on-call @siva. Add me if needs escalation.

siva: Got it. I'll monitor canary overnight.

alex_m: Thanks team.
